The coverage map below leaves the proposed plan unchanged. Ticket labels are provisional.

| Requirement or decision | Source | Coverage | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read volunteers and unavailable days from CSV | README | B: CSV inputs; E: CLI | Valid files load; malformed rows, duplicate names, and invalid days produce clear errors |
| Respect whole-day unavailability | Your decision | D: Scheduling | No assignment falls on a volunteer’s unavailable day |
| Fair means assignment counts differ by at most one | README | D: Scheduling | Feasible examples satisfy this across all listed volunteers, including those assigned zero |
| When fairness is impossible, print the fairest rota and list who is over | Your decision | D: Optimization; E: Reporting | Small exhaustive reference cases establish optimality; output names overloaded volunteers and their excess |
| Print the weekly rota | README | E: CLI | End-to-end tests verify assignments, totals, overloads, and unfilled shifts |
| One organiser runs locally; retain Python | Your decision | B, D, E | `python -m rota` works with local input files without a network service |
| Specify shifts in a separate CSV | Proposed default under delegated judgement | B, E | Unique shift IDs and valid days load; multiple shifts per day remain distinct |
| Maximize filled shifts before optimizing fairness | Proposed default under delegated judgement | D | Reference cases verify coverage takes priority; unavailable shifts remain explicitly unfilled |
| Define “over” as exceeding the minimum volunteer count plus one | Proposed default under delegated judgement | D, E | Reported names and excess counts match computed assignments |
| Handle empty inputs and invalid files clearly | Proposed default under delegated judgement | B, E | Empty shifts produce an empty rota; no volunteers or invalid input produce errors |
| Preserve evidence of existing round-robin behavior | `rota/schedule.py`, `tests/test_schedule.py` | A: Completed baseline | Source and test inspection; no claim that tests have run |
| Review usability before CLI implementation | Proposed owner checkpoint | C, blocking E | You review sample CSVs and proposed output |
| Accept the complete first version | Proposed owner checkpoint | F, after E | Demonstration covers fair, unfair, unfillable, and invalid-input cases |
| Email volunteers their shifts | README: later scope | Explicitly deferred | No first-version implementation |
| Balance workloads across multiple weeks | Proposed scope boundary | Explicitly excluded | Fairness applies to the supplied week only |

Checkpoint tickets record owner reviews but do not mechanically enforce approval.
